site.title: Chanoch and the Name Within Him
site.subtitle: On Enoch, Metatron, Havayah HaKatan, the Returning Human, and the Torah of a World Ready to Receive Him
site.description: A cinematic study of Chanoch ben Yered and Metatron across Torah, Chazal, Heikhalot literature, Kabbalah and Chassidus — read through bittul, Malchus and dirah betachtonim.
site.keywords: Chanoch, Enoch, Metatron, Sar HaPanim, Havayah HaKatan, Malchus, bittul, dirah betachtonim, Kabbalah, Chassidus, Heikhalot

hero.thesis: Chanoch walks upward. Metatron receives from above. Malchus receives and returns. The circuit closes when heaven can dwell below.
hero.standfirst: The Torah says almost nothing about him. Precisely because it says almost nothing, the words it does say refuse to close.

modes.experienceBlurb: Thirteen acts and a finale, moving through concealment, walking, ascent, fire, crown, Name, service, reception, return and dwelling.
modes.studyBlurb: The complete maamar — fifty-one chapters, with source layers, original Hebrew and Aramaic quotations, and a glossary.
modes.officeBlurb: The titles and offices of the Great Servant, each one shown as received rather than self-originating.
modes.circuitBlurb: Or yashar descends, the receiver answers, or chozer rises. An interactive account of active reception.

study.title: Study Mode
study.endOfEssayNote: Chanoch walked upward before the circuit was complete. Metatron remembers the path.

office.title: The Celestial Office
office.intro: Every title below is an office held, not a nature possessed. The constellation is arranged so that the closer a dignity stands to the centre, the more transparent it becomes: greatness here is rendered as clarity, not as opacity.
office.paradox: The greater the office, the deeper the bittul. The more that passes through him, the less he claims to be its source.
office.selectPrompt: Select a dignity to open it.
office.guardrail: Metatron is a created being. Nothing on this page presents him as G-d, as a second authority, or as an object of prayer.

circuit.title: The Malchus Circuit
circuit.openingTranslation: She has nothing of her own.
circuit.intro: Having nothing of one’s own is not poverty. It is the condition that makes it possible to receive everything without pretending to have originated it — and then to answer.
circuit.analogyNotice: Analogy, not identity. Metatron is never equated with the Shechinah or with Malchus. The comparison illuminates the structure of reception; it does not merge the two.

stages.descent: Or yashar — the direct light descends
stages.return: Or chozer — the returning light rises
stages.dwelling: The circuit closes; the lower world becomes a dwelling

circuit.metaphorPrompt: Choose a facet. Each explains the same principle from a different side.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.eyebrow: Terms kept in their own language
glossary.intro: Sacred and technical vocabulary is preserved rather than flattened into approximate equivalents. Each term is glossed on first use.

sources.title: Sources and Layers
sources.eyebrow: How this site distinguishes its claims
sources.intro: Different Jewish texts describe the celestial order differently. This site keeps those layers visible rather than flattening them into a single voice. A later mystical claim is never presented as though it were stated explicitly in Bereishis.
sources.citationPolicyBody: Works and traditions are cited at the level this project can responsibly verify. Where an exact folio or page reference has not been confirmed, the work or tradition is named instead. No page citations have been invented.

Motion is authored with GSAP and a small hand-written WebGL layer, and is disabled wherever the reader has asked for less of it.
footer.editorialNoteBody: English is the source of truth for this text. Translations aim to read as native compositions. Source-layer labels are part of the argument, not decoration.
footer.rights: This study is offered for learning.
